claim: The crystal structure of Chlamydomonas IFT-B protein IFT80 was determined at 1.8 Å resolution.
source: Here we present the 1.8 Å resolution crystal structure of the Chlamydomonas IFT-B protein IFT80, which reveals the architecture of two N-terminal β-propellers followed by an α-helical extension.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the resolution of the crystal structure and the organism from which IFT80 was derived.

claim: IFT80 contains two N-terminal β-propellers followed by an α-helical extension.
source: Here we present the 1.8 Å resolution crystal structure of the Chlamydomonas IFT-B protein IFT80, which reveals the architecture of two N-terminal β-propellers followed by an α-helical extension.
evidence: The structural architecture is directly stated in the abstract and supported by crystallographic data.

claim: The N-terminal β-propeller of IFT80 tethers it to the IFT-B complex via IFT38.
source: The N-terminal β-propeller tethers IFT80 to the IFT-B complex via IFT38 whereas the second β-propeller and the C-terminal α-helical extension result in IFT80 homo-dimerization.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this interaction, which is supported by biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The second β-propeller and C-terminal α-helical extension of IFT80 result in homo-dimerization.
source: The N-terminal β-propeller tethers IFT80 to the IFT-B complex via IFT38 whereas the second β-propeller and the C-terminal α-helical extension result in IFT80 homo-dimerization.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this structural feature, which is supported by crystallographic and biophysical data.

claim: Biallelic Ift80 frameshift mutations in IMCD3 mouse cells were created using CRISPR/Cas.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas to create biallelic Ift80 frameshift mutations in IMCD3 mouse cells, we demonstrate that IFT80 is absolutely required for ciliogenesis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the method used to generate mutations.

claim: IFT80 is absolutely required for ciliogenesis.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas to create biallelic Ift80 frameshift mutations in IMCD3 mouse cells, we demonstrate that IFT80 is absolutely required for ciliogenesis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion based on knockout experiments.

claim: Human disease-causing missense mutations in IFT80 do not cluster within the protein structure.
source: Structural mapping and rescue experiments reveal that human disease-causing missense mutations do not cluster within IFT80 and form functional IFT particles.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on structural mapping.

claim: Missense mutant forms of IFT80 form functional IFT particles.
source: Structural mapping and rescue experiments reveal that human disease-causing missense mutations do not cluster within IFT80 and form functional IFT particles.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on rescue experiments.

claim: Deletion of the C-terminal dimerization domain of IFT80 prevented rescue of ciliogenesis.
source: Unlike missense mutant forms of IFT80, deletion of the C-terminal dimerization domain prevented rescue of ciliogenesis.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from rescue experiments.

claim: IFT80 dimerization may provide insight into higher order IFT complex formation required for IFT train formation.
source: Taken together our results may provide a first insight into higher order IFT complex formation likely required for IFT train formation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a speculative conclusion based on the structural and functional data.

claim: Cilia and flagella are eukaryotic cellular organelles important for motility, sensory reception, and developmental signalling.
source: Cilia and flagella are eukaryotic cellular organelles important for motility, sensory reception, and developmental signalling (Ishikawa and Marshall, 2011), and defects in ciliary structure and/or function result in human pathologies collectively known as 'ciliopathies' (Fliegauf et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Defects in ciliary structure and/or function result in human pathologies collectively known as 'ciliopathies'.
source: Cilia and flagella are eukaryotic cellular organelles important for motility, sensory reception, and developmental signalling (Ishikawa and Marshall, 2011), and defects in ciliary structure and/or function result in human pathologies collectively known as 'ciliopathies' (Fliegauf et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and Trypanosoma brucei serve as model organisms for ciliary studies.
source: Cilia are found on most cells in mammals, as well as on unicellular organisms such as Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (Cr) and Trypanosoma brucei (Tb) that serve as model organisms for ciliary studies (Vincensini et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: With only very few exceptions, cilia are built by intraflagellar transport (IFT).
source: With only very few exceptions, cilia are built by intraflagellar transport (IFT), the bi-directional movement of proteinaceous material sandwiched between the microtubule (MT)-based axoneme and the ciliary membrane (Kozminski et al., 1993; Rosenbaum and Witman, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to foundational literature on IFT.

claim: IFT is the bi-directional movement of proteinaceous material sandwiched between the microtubule-based axoneme and the ciliary membrane.
source: With only very few exceptions, cilia are built by intraflagellar transport (IFT), the bi-directional movement of proteinaceous material sandwiched between the microtubule (MT)-based axoneme and the ciliary membrane (Kozminski et al., 1993; Rosenbaum and Witman, 2002).
evidence: This definition is supported by citations to foundational literature.

claim: The process of IFT in Chlamydomonas requires a 22 subunit IFT particle.
source: The process of IFT in Chlamydomonas requires the 22 subunit IFT particle that associates with the hetero-trimeric kinesin 2 or cytoplasmic dynein 2 motors for anterograde (ciliary base to tip) or retrograde (ciliary tip to base) transport of cargo proteins, respectively.
evidence: This statement describes the composition of the IFT particle based on established knowledge.

claim: The IFT particle associates with heterotrimeric kinesin 2 for anterograde transport of cargo proteins.
source: The process of IFT in Chlamydomonas requires the 22 subunit IFT particle that associates with the hetero-trimeric kinesin 2 or cytoplasmic dynein 2 motors for anterograde (ciliary base to tip) or retrograde (ciliary tip to base) transport of cargo proteins, respectively.
evidence: This statement describes the motor protein association based on established knowledge.

claim: The IFT particle associates with cytoplasmic dynein 2 motors for retrograde transport of cargo proteins.
source: The process of IFT in Chlamydomonas requires the 22 subunit IFT particle that associates with the hetero-trimeric kinesin 2 or cytoplasmic dynein 2 motors for anterograde (ciliary base to tip) or retrograde (ciliary tip to base) transport of cargo proteins, respectively.
evidence: This statement describes the motor protein association based on established knowledge.

claim: In C. elegans sensory cilia, a homo-dimeric kinesin 2 (OSM-3) cooperates with heterotrimeric kinesin 2 to drive anterograde IFT.
source: In C. elegans sensory cilia the situation is more complex, as a homo-dimeric kinesin 2 (OSM-3) cooperates with heterotrimeric kinesin 2 to drive anterograde IFT (Snow et al., 2004; Prevo et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature on C. elegans IFT.

claim: The IFT particle consists of a six subunit IFT-A and a 16 subunit IFT-B complex.
source: The IFT particle consists of a six subunit IFT-A and a 16 subunit IFT-B complex, with the latter further divided into a 10 subunit IFT-B1 and a 6-subunit IFT-B2 sub-complex (Taschner et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes the composition of the IFT particle and is supported by a citation.

claim: IFT-B complex is further divided into a 10 subunit IFT-B1 and a 6-subunit IFT-B2 sub-complex.
source: The IFT particle consists of a six subunit IFT-A and a 16 subunit IFT-B complex, with the latter further divided into a 10 subunit IFT-B1 and a 6-subunit IFT-B2 sub-complex (Taschner et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes the sub-complex organization and is supported by a citation.

claim: IFT-A and IFT-B complexes dissociate even at low salt concentration when isolated from Chlamydomonas flagella.
source: Whereas IFT-A and IFT-B complexes dissociate even at low salt concentration when isolated from Cr flagella (Cole et al., 1998), IFT-B1 and IFT-B2 sub-complexes associate strongly to form a stable IFT-B complex that can be reconstituted from recombinantly produced subunits (Taschner et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature on IFT complex stability.

claim: IFT-B1 and IFT-B2 sub-complexes associate strongly to form a stable IFT-B complex that can be reconstituted from recombinantly produced subunits.
source: Whereas IFT-A and IFT-B complexes dissociate even at low salt concentration when isolated from Cr flagella (Cole et al., 1998), IFT-B1 and IFT-B2 sub-complexes associate strongly to form a stable IFT-B complex that can be reconstituted from recombinantly produced subunits (Taschner et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature on IFT complex reconstitution.

claim: Electron tomographic reconstructions reveal that IFT particles organize into long strings known as IFT trains in Chlamydomonas flagella.
source: Electron tomographic reconstructions of IFT material in situ reveal that IFT particles organize into long strings known as IFT trains in Chlamydomonas flagella (Pigino et al., 2009; Vannuccini et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to electron tomography studies.

claim: IFT trains have been observed in Trypanosoma.
source: IFT trains have also been observed in Trypanosoma (Absalon et al., 2008) and in some cases in human primary cilia (Rogowski et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature on Trypanosoma IFT.

claim: IFT trains have been observed in some cases in human primary cilia.
source: IFT trains have also been observed in Trypanosoma (Absalon et al., 2008) and in some cases in human primary cilia (Rogowski et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature on human primary cilia.

claim: IFT proteins are sequentially recruited at the basal body to form IFT trains that are loaded with tubulin cargo shortly before departure.
source: IFT proteins are sequentially recruited at the basal body to form IFT trains that are loaded with tubulin cargo shortly before departure (Wingfield et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to literature on IFT train assembly.

claim: Anterograde and retrograde IFT trains travel on different tubules of the axonemal MT-doublets in Chlamydomonas flagella.
source: An elegant study coupling total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) and electron microscopy recently revealed that anterograde and retrograde IFT trains travel on different tubules of the axonemal MT-doublets in Chlamydomonas flagella, providing an explanation for the absence of head-to-head collisions of IFT trains (Stepanek and Pigino, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a study combining TIRF and electron microscopy.

claim: The travel of anterograde and retrograde IFT trains on different tubules provides an explanation for the absence of head-to-head collisions of IFT trains.
source: An elegant study coupling total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) and electron microscopy recently revealed that anterograde and retrograde IFT trains travel on different tubules of the axonemal MT-doublets in Chlamydomonas flagella, providing an explanation for the absence of head-to-head collisions of IFT trains (Stepanek and Pigino, 2016).
evidence: This statement is an inference drawn from the cited study.

claim: Two morphologically different types of short arrays (~200 nm in length, 16 nm repeat) with IFT particle volumes of ~5000 nm3 correspond to moving anterograde and retrograde trains.
source: Two morphologically different types of short (~200 nm in length, 16 nm repeat) arrays with IFT particle volumes of ~5000 nm3 correspond to the moving anterograde and retrograde trains (Pigino et al., 2009; Vannuccini et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to electron tomography studies.

claim: A longer IFT train type (~650 nm in length, 40 nm repeat) with two IFT particles related by 2-fold symmetry and a volume of ~10000 nm3 was identified as a 'standing' train not moving in either direction.
source: Additionally, a longer (~650 nm in length, 40 nm repeat) IFT train type with two IFT particles related by 2-fold symmetry and a volume of ~10000 nm3 was identified as a 'standing' train not moving in either direction (Pigino et al., 2009; Stepanek and Pigino, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to electron tomography studies.

claim: It is currently not known how IFT particles associate to form different types of IFT trains.
source: It is currently not known how IFT particles associate to form either of these different types of IFT trains.
evidence: This statement explicitly acknowledges a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Significant progress has been made in understanding IFT complex composition from studies of material obtained directly from Chlamydomonas flagella.
source: Since the discovery of the IFT complex in Chlamydomonas two decades ago, significant progress has been made in understanding its composition from studies of material obtained directly from Cr flagella (Cole et al., 1998; Piperno and Mead, 1997; Lucker et al., 2005; Behal and Cole, 2013; Richey and Qin, 2012), as well as from work using recombinantly expressed proteins (Taschner et al., 2016; Lucker et al., 2010; Taschner et al., 2011; Taschner et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to literature on IFT complex composition.

claim: An increasing number of crystal structures provide a detailed view of several parts of the IFT transport machinery.
source: Furthermore, an increasing number of crystal structures provide us with a detailed view of several parts of this sophisticated transport machinery (Taschner et al., 2016; Taschner et al., 2014; Bhogaraju et al., 2011; Bhogaraju et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: None of the previous studies have provided clues about how IFT complexes form larger assemblies.
source: However, none of these studies have so far provided any clues about how IFT complexes form larger assemblies, which presumably relies on the ability of one or several IFT proteins to oligomerize.
evidence: This statement explicitly identifies a gap in previous research.

claim: Formation of larger IFT assemblies presumably relies on the ability of one or several IFT proteins to oligomerize.
source: However, none of these studies have so far provided any clues about how IFT complexes form larger assemblies, which presumably relies on the ability of one or several IFT proteins to oligomerize.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the lack of previous findings.

claim: The hexameric IFT-B2 complex was recently identified in several studies.
source: The hexameric IFT-B2 complex was recently identified in several studies (Taschner et al., 2016; Boldt et al., 2016; Katoh et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Missense mutations in IFT80 have been identified in individuals with Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (JATD).
source: Missense mutations in IFT80, which encodes an IFT-B2 subunit, have been identified in individuals with the skeletal ciliopathies Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (JATD) as well as Verma-Naumoff syndrome (Baujat et al., 2013; Beales et al., 2007; Cavalcanti et al., 2011), but it is still unclear how these alterations affect protein function.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to clinical literature.

claim: Missense mutations in IFT80 have been identified in individuals with Verma-Naumoff syndrome.
source: Missense mutations in IFT80, which encodes an IFT-B2 subunit, have been identified in individuals with the skeletal ciliopathies Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (JATD) as well as Verma-Naumoff syndrome (Baujat et al., 2013; Beales et al., 2007; Cavalcanti et al., 2011), but it is still unclear how these alterations affect protein function.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to clinical literature.

claim: It is still unclear how IFT80 missense mutations affect protein function.
source: Missense mutations in IFT80, which encodes an IFT-B2 subunit, have been identified in individuals with the skeletal ciliopathies Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (JATD) as well as Verma-Naumoff syndrome (Baujat et al., 2013; Beales et al., 2007; Cavalcanti et al., 2011), but it is still unclear how these alterations affect protein function.
evidence: This statement explicitly acknowledges a gap in understanding.

claim: Previous gene knockdown studies of Ift80 using RNA interference in mammalian cell culture have reported a quantitative reduction, but incomplete loss, of axonemal acetylated tubulin of primary and motile cilia.
source: Previous gene knockdown studies of Ift80, which have used RNA interference in mammalian cell culture or conditional gene-targeting in mice, have reported a quantitative reduction, but incomplete loss, of axonemal acetylated tubulin of primary and motile cilia (Beales et al., 2007; Yuan and Yang, 2015; Yuan et al., 2016; Yang and Wang, 2012; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous knockdown studies.

claim: A constitutional hypomorphic Ift80 gene-trap mouse model faithfully recapitulated features of JATD without affecting cilia formation.
source: A constitutional hypomorphic Ift80 gene-trap mouse model faithfully recapitulated features of JATD without affecting cilia formation (Rix et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a mouse model study.

claim: It is unclear whether IFT80 is absolutely required for IFT mediated recruitment and transport of ciliary cargo.
source: It is therefore unclear whether IFT80 is absolutely required for IFT mediated recruitment and transport of ciliary cargo.
evidence: This statement explicitly acknowledges uncertainty based on previous studies.

claim: It has been speculated that IFT80 missense mutations may be hypomorphic.
source: It has also been speculated that IFT80 missense mutations may be hypomorphic although this remains to be proven.
evidence: This statement explicitly identifies a speculation that has not been proven.

claim: IFT80 adopts the fold of two consecutive seven bladed β-propellers followed by an alpha-solenoid extension of 4 α-helices.
source: In the crystal structure, IFT80 adopts the fold of two consecutive seven bladed β-propellers followed by an alpha-solenoid extension of 4 α-helices.
evidence: This statement describes the structural fold observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The 4 α-helices of IFT80 organize into two tetratricopeptide (TPR)-like repeats.
source: These helices organize into two tetratricopeptide (TPR)-like repeats, and are held in position via interactions with an extension of blade 6 of BP2.
evidence: This statement describes the structural organization observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The α-helices are held in position via interactions with an extension of blade 6 of BP2.
source: These helices organize into two tetratricopeptide (TPR)-like repeats, and are held in position via interactions with an extension of blade 6 of BP2.
evidence: This statement describes structural interactions observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The extension of blade 6 of BP2 contains an insertion of two α-helices, which are held in place by largely hydrophobic contacts with BP2 blade 5.
source: This extension contains an insertion of two α-helices, which are themselves held in place by largely hydrophobic contacts with BP2 blade 5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement describes structural features observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The C-terminal 126 residues of full-length IFT80 have no visible electron density and are presumably disordered in the crystal.
source: Although the fl IFT80 protein was crystallized (verified by mass spectrometry), the C-terminal 126 residues have no visible electron density and are presumably disordered in the crystal.
evidence: This statement describes an observation from the crystal structure and makes an inference about disorder.

claim: The C-terminal region of IFT80 is efficiently removed by incubation with all four proteases tested.
source: Our finding that this region is efficiently removed by incubation with all four proteases tested (Figure 1D) supports this assumption.
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The missing C-terminal residues of IFT80 are predicted to adopt the structure of seven α-helices.
source: The missing residues are predicted to adopt the structure of seven α-helices and are connected to the four visible helices by a well-conserved 15 amino acid long linker region (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement describes a prediction based on sequence analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: BP1 of IFT80 adopts the fold of a canonical seven bladed β-propeller where the N-terminal residues contribute the first β-strand to blade 7.
source: BP1 adopts the fold of a canonical seven bladed β-propeller where the N-terminal residues contribute the first β-strand to blade 7, effectively closing the β-propeller by a zipper-like mechanism (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement describes structural features observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: BP1 of IFT80 displays high structural similarity to the N-terminal β-propellers of β'-COP, β-COP and α-COP.
source: BP1 of IFT80 is thus similar to a number of previously determined structures of β-propellers, and displays particularly high structural similarity to the N-terminal β-propellers of β'-COP, β-COP and α-COP, which are coatomer subunits important in the formation of COP-coated vesicles (Lee and Goldberg, 2010).
evidence: This statement describes structural comparison and is supported by a citation.

claim: BP1 of IFT80 and β'-COP share ~15% sequence identity.
source: Although BP1 of IFT80 and β'-COP only share ~15% sequence identity, the domains superimpose well with a root-mean-square-deviation (rmsd) of 2.2 Å over ~300 residues (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement describes sequence comparison data.

claim: BP1 of IFT80 and β'-COP superimpose well with a root-mean-square-deviation (rmsd) of 2.2 Å over ~300 residues.
source: Although BP1 of IFT80 and β'-COP only share ~15% sequence identity, the domains superimpose well with a root-mean-square-deviation (rmsd) of 2.2 Å over ~300 residues (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement describes structural comparison data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The high degree of structural similarity between IFT80 BP1 and coatomer subunits is consistent with the notion that IFT80 evolved from a coatomer-like progenitor.
source: This high degree of structural similarity is consistent with the notion that IFT80 evolved from a coatomer-like progenitor (Jékely and Arendt, 2006; van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement makes an inference about evolution supported by citations.

claim: In the IFT80 structure, the most C-terminal β-strand of BP1 connects to BP2 as one long continuous β-strand.
source: Firstly, in the IFT80 structure, the most C-terminal β-strand of BP1 connects to BP2 as one long continuous β-strand (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement describes a structural feature observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In β'-COP, BP1 and BP2 are connected via a loop.
source: This is quite different from β'-COP where BP1 and BP2 are connected via a loop (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement describes a structural feature of β'-COP shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The structural divergence in the connection between BP1 and BP2 positions BP2 differently relative to BP1 in IFT80 and β'-COP.
source: This structural divergence is important as it positions BP2 differently relative to BP1 in the two structures (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement makes an inference about the structural consequence shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The extended loop that connects β-strands 3 and 4 of blade 1 and closes BP2 in β'-COP is missing in IFT80.
source: Secondly, the extended loop that connects β-strands 3 and 4 of blade 1, and interacts with the last strand in blade seven to effectively close BP2 in β'-COP, is missing in IFT80 (compare Figure 2C–2E).
evidence: This statement describes a structural difference observed by comparing figures.

claim: BP2 of IFT80 adopts an unusual open conformation where blades 1 and 7 do not interact.
source: This structural difference results in an unusual open conformation of BP2 of IFT80 where blades 1 and 7 do not interact (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement describes a structural feature observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The C-terminal α-helical extensions are found on opposite sides in the structures of IFT80 and β'-COP.
source: Because of the very different positions of BP2 in IFT80 and β'-COP, the C-terminal α-helical extensions are found on opposite sides in the structures (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement describes a structural comparison shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Despite similar domain composition, the relative 3D orientation of domains in IFT80 and coatomer subunits is remarkably different.
source: Thus, despite the similar domain composition of IFT80 and coatomer subunits, the relative 3D orientation of domains is remarkably different.
evidence: This statement summarizes the structural comparison.

claim: IFT80 is unlikely to function directly in the coating of vesicles destined for the cilium.
source: Given the structural divergence, IFT80 is unlikely to function directly in the coating of vesicles destined for the cilium.
evidence: This statement makes an inference based on the structural divergence from coatomer proteins.

claim: IFT80 BP1 is sufficient for complex formation with the IFT38 CH-domain.
source: The result of this experiment shows that IFT80 BP1 is sufficient for complex formation with the IFT38 CH-domain.
evidence: This statement describes the result of a GST pull-down experiment.

claim: A complex of IFT80(BP1) and the IFT38 CH-domain could be reconstituted and purified by SEC.
source: Indeed, a complex of IFT80(BP1) and the IFT38 CH-domain could be reconstituted and purified by SEC (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: IFT80-IFT38 is a stoichiometric complex with a dissociation constant (Kd) of ~225 nM.
source: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) of the CH-domain of IFT38 and the BP1-BP2 construct of IFT80 (this construct was chosen as it displayed the best behaviour in ITC assays) revealed that IFT80-IFT38 is a stoichiometric complex with a dissociation constant (Kd) of ~225 nM (Figure 3D).
evidence: This statement describes ITC data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The IFT80-IFT54/20 interaction requires the C-terminal α-helical extension of IFT80.
source: Here, we show that this interaction requires the C-terminal α-helical extension of IFT80 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: The IFT80-IFT54/20 interaction does not require the N-terminal tubulin-binding CH-domain of IFT54.
source: The IFT80-IFT54/20 interaction does not require the N-terminal tubulin-binding CH-domain of IFT54 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and only very weak binding was observed between IFT801-654 and IFT54ΔCH/20 demonstrating that the association depends on the 111 most C-terminal residues of IFT80 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The IFT80-IFT54/20 association depends on the 111 most C-terminal residues of IFT80.
source: The IFT80-IFT54/20 interaction does not require the N-terminal tubulin-binding CH-domain of IFT54 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and only very weak binding was observed between IFT801-654 and IFT54ΔCH/20 demonstrating that the association depends on the 111 most C-terminal residues of IFT80 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement describes an inference from experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: IFT80 is incorporated into the IFT complex mainly via a strong interaction of the BP1 domain with the IFT38 CH-domain.
source: We conclude that IFT80 is incorporated into the IFT complex mainly via a strong interaction of the BP1 domain with the IFT38 CH-domain but displays additional interactions between the IFT80 C-terminus and the IFT54/20 complex.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the biochemical data presented.

claim: IFT80 displays additional interactions between the IFT80 C-terminus and the IFT54/20 complex.
source: We conclude that IFT80 is incorporated into the IFT complex mainly via a strong interaction of the BP1 domain with the IFT38 CH-domain but displays additional interactions between the IFT80 C-terminus and the IFT54/20 complex.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the biochemical data presented.

claim: The crystal structure of IFT80 revealed an IFT80 homo-dimer organized around a crystallographic 2-fold axis.
source: Inspection of the crystal packing of the IFT80 structure presented here revealed an IFT80 homo-dimer organized around a crystallographic 2-fold axis (Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement describes an observation from the crystal structure shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The unusual position of the C-terminal BP2 and α-helical domains allows IFT80 to homo-dimerize via an extended interaction interface.
source: The unusual position of the C-terminal BP2 and α-helical domains outlined above and shown in Figure 2 allows IFT80 to homo-dimerize via an extended interaction interface contributed by BP2 and the α-helical C-terminal domain.
evidence: This statement makes an inference about the structural basis of dimerization.

claim: Two separate interaction interfaces contribute to IFT80 dimerization.
source: Two separate interaction interfaces contribute to IFT80 dimerization.
evidence: This statement describes structural features observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The first dimerization interface is a 6-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet where blade 7 of each BP2 domain contributes three β-strands.
source: The first is a 6-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet where blade 7 of each BP2 domain contributes three β-strands (solid rounded rectangle in Figure 4A, and zoom-in in Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement describes a structural feature observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Two residues (L575 and S577) in β-strand 54 make backbone interactions with their symmetry mates to keep the β-sheet aligned.
source: Two residues (L575 and S577) in β-strand 54 make backbone interactions with their symmetry mates (partially mediated by water molecules) to keep the resulting β-sheet aligned (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement describes structural interactions observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The second dimerization interface is formed by interactions of the first TPR-like repeat (alpha helices α4−α5) in the α-solenoid domain with blade 1 of BP2.
source: The second interface (present in two copies in the dimer due to symmetry) is formed by interactions of the first TPR-like repeat (alpha helices α4−α5) in the α-solenoid domain with blade 1 of BP2 (dashed rounded rectangles in Figure 4A, and zoom-in in Figure 4C).
evidence: This statement describes a structural feature observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Only one of the contacts in the second dimerization interface is hydrophobic in nature (F605 in a hydrophobic pocket formed by R316 and E329).
source: Only one of the contacts here is hydrophobic in nature (F605 is located in a hydrophobic pocket formed by the aliphatic parts of the side chains of R316 and E329), all other interactions are hydrophilic and partially water-mediated, and also involve several backbone interactions (Figure 4C).
evidence: This statement describes structural interactions observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The entire interaction interface between two IFT80 monomers has a combined buried surface area of ~1200 Å2.
source: Taken together, the entire interaction interface between two IFT80 monomers (1x 'interface 1' and 2x 'interface 2') has a combined buried surface area of ~1200 Å2.
evidence: This statement describes a calculated value from the crystal structure.

claim: IFT80 eluted as a dimer at low salt conditions (150 mM NaCl) in SEC experiments.
source: In SEC experiments, IFT80 eluted as a dimer at low salt conditions (150 mM NaCl), but as a monomer at higher salt concentrations (500 mM NaCl, Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: IFT80 eluted as a monomer at higher salt concentrations (500 mM NaCl) in SEC experiments.
source: In SEC experiments, IFT80 eluted as a dimer at low salt conditions (150 mM NaCl), but as a monomer at higher salt concentrations (500 mM NaCl, Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SAXS measurements indicated that the molecular dimensions of IFT80 were larger in low salt than in high salt.
source: The measurements indicated that the molecular dimensions of the IFT80 protein were larger in low salt than in high salt (Figure 5B and Table 2), again suggesting that high salt converts the IFT80 dimer into monomers.
evidence: This statement describes SAXS data shown in Figure 5B and Table 2.

claim: The SAXS envelope obtained in low salt conditions showed a better fit to the crystal structure of the IFT80 dimer (χ2 of 0.947) than to the monomer (χ2 of 4.419).
source: Consistent with this, the SAXS envelope obtained in low salt conditions showed a significantly better fit to the crystal structure of the IFT80 dimer (χ2 of 0.947) than to that of the monomer (χ2 of 4.419) (Figure 5C), whereas the opposite was the case for the data obtained in high salt (χ2of 1.589 for dimer, χ2 of 1.187 for monomer) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This statement describes SAXS data analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The SAXS envelope obtained in high salt conditions showed a better fit to the crystal structure of the IFT80 monomer (χ2 of 1.187) than to the dimer (χ2 of 1.589).
source: Consistent with this, the SAXS envelope obtained in low salt conditions showed a significantly better fit to the crystal structure of the IFT80 dimer (χ2 of 0.947) than to that of the monomer (χ2 of 4.419) (Figure 5C), whereas the opposite was the case for the data obtained in high salt (χ2of 1.589 for dimer, χ2 of 1.187 for monomer) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This statement describes SAXS data analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: IFT80 exists as a dimer in solution at physiological salt concentrations.
source: Taken together these results confirm that IFT80 exists as a dimer in solution at physiological salt concentrations.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from SEC and SAXS data.

claim: IFT80(1-654) is a dimer in SEC experiments under low salt conditions.
source: The result show that IFT80(1-654) is a dimer whereas IFT80(BP1-BP2) is a monomer (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: IFT80(BP1-BP2) is a monomer in SEC experiments under low salt conditions.
source: The result show that IFT80(1-654) is a dimer whereas IFT80(BP1-BP2) is a monomer (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: DLS measurements of IFT80(BP1-BP2) resulted in a constant ~3.6 nm radius independently of protein concentration.
source: Consistent with the assumption that the BP1-BP2 construct of IFT80 is monomeric, DLS measurements resulted in a constant ~3.6 nm radius of the molecule independently of protein concentration (Figure 6A, left).
evidence: This statement describes DLS data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The radius obtained for full-length IFT80 by DLS changed with increasing protein concentration, starting just below 4 nm at the lowest concentration and reaching a plateau around ~5.5 nm.
source: In contrast, the obtained radius for the full-length protein changed with increasing protein concentration, starting just below 4 nm at the lowest concentration examined, and reaching a plateau around ~5.5 nm when the concentration was increased (Figure 6A, right).
evidence: This statement describes DLS data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A 14-subunit IFT-B complex containing IFT80 was assembled and purified.
source: To address if dimerization might also occur in an IFT80-containing IFT-B complex, we assembled a 14-subunit IFT-B complex containing a 9-subunit IFT-B1 complex (IFT88/71/74/70/52/46/27/25/22) (Taschner et al., 2014) and a 5-subunit IFT-B2 complex (IFT80/57/54/38/20) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This statement describes the reconstitution of a complex shown in Figure 6C.

claim: DLS and SAXS measurements of the 14-subunit IFT-B complex revealed a concentration-dependent increase in the radius of the complex from ~10 nm to approximately 15 nm.
source: Both DLS (Figure 6D) and SAXS measurements (Figure 6E) over a range of concentrations of this 14-meric IFT-B complex revealed results paralleling those of fl IFT80 alone, with a concentration-dependent increase in the radius of the complex from a starting value of ~10 nm to a plateau at a value of approximately 15 nm.
evidence: This statement describes DLS and SAXS data shown in Figures 6D and 6E.

claim: The concentration-dependent behavior of the 14-subunit IFT-B complex suggests a transition from monomeric to dimeric complexes.
source: The values are, however, compatible with a concentration dependent transition from monomeric to dimeric 14-subunit IFT-B complexes.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the DLS and SAXS data.

claim: IFT80 is capable of organizing dimers of IFT-B complexes consistent with the multimerization of IFT particles into train-like structures observed in situ.
source: The fact that the concentration-dependent behaviour of the 14-subunit IFT-B complex is similar to isolated IFT80 suggests that IFT80 is capable of organizing dimers of IFT-B complexes consistent with the multimerization of IFT particles in to train-like structures observed in situ (Kozminski et al., 1993; Pigino et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is an inference from the biophysical data and is supported by citations to in situ observations.

claim: Clonal IMCD3 cell lines carrying biallelic frameshift mutations in mouse Ift80 were generated using gene-editing.
source: We used gene-editing to achieve total gene knockout by generating clonal IMCD3 cell lines carrying biallelic frameshift mutations in mouse Ift80 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the generation of knockout cell lines shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: One IMCD3 clone was compound heterozygous for p.T24fsX32/p.V20fsX29 mutations in Ift80.
source: Using a gRNA targeting exon 3, we isolated one clone that was compound heterozygous for p.T24fsX32/p.V20fsX29 mutations, as judged by direct sequencing and T7 endonuclease I assay (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement describes genotyping data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Both p.T24fsX32 and p.V20fsX29 alleles are predicted to cause premature termination at the start of BP1.
source: Both alleles are predicted to cause premature termination at the start of BP1.
evidence: This statement is a prediction based on the mutation positions.

claim: Serum-starvation of control wild-type IMCD3 cells for 48 hr resulted in robust formation of primary cilia.
source: Serum-starvation of control wild-type cells for 48 hr resulted in robust formation of primary cilia.
evidence: This statement describes experimental observations.

claim: Cilia completely failed to form in the Ift80 mutant cell line.
source: By contrast, cilia completely failed to form in the Ift80 mutant cell line – 100% of mutant cells displayed absolutely no acetylated tubulin staining, while a single γ-tubulin + basal body could be seen overlaid by a small amount of Arl13b + ciliary membrane (Figures 7A and 8A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental observations shown in Figures 7A and 8A.

claim: 100% of Ift80 mutant cells displayed absolutely no acetylated tubulin staining.
source: By contrast, cilia completely failed to form in the Ift80 mutant cell line – 100% of mutant cells displayed absolutely no acetylated tubulin staining, while a single γ-tubulin + basal body could be seen overlaid by a small amount of Arl13b + ciliary membrane (Figures 7A and 8A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental observations shown in Figures 7A and 8A.

claim: Ift80 mutant cells retained a single γ-tubulin positive basal body overlaid by a small amount of Arl13b positive ciliary membrane.
source: By contrast, cilia completely failed to form in the Ift80 mutant cell line – 100% of mutant cells displayed absolutely no acetylated tubulin staining, while a single γ-tubulin + basal body could be seen overlaid by a small amount of Arl13b + ciliary membrane (Figures 7A and 8A).
evidence: This statement describes experimental observations shown in Figures 7A and 8A.

claim: mIFT80-GFP was observed within IFT trains using super-resolution fluorescence microscopy.
source: Using super-resolution fluorescence microscopy, we observed mIFT80-GFP (stained using an anti-GFP antibody) within IFT trains, which punctuated the length of the cilium (Figure 7B).
evidence: This statement describes microscopy observations shown in Figure 7B.

claim: There was an average of 21.8 ± 9.6 (95% CI) IFT80-GFP particles per cilium separated by 0.33 ± 0.15 µm (95% CI).
source: There was an average of 21.8 ± 9.6 (95% CI) particles per cilium separated by 0.33 ± 0.15 µm (95% CI).
evidence: This statement describes quantitative microscopy data.

claim: mIFT80-GFP rescued ciliogenesis in Ift80 null-mutant cells to the same degree as an untagged construct.
source: This tagged form of IFT80 was functional, rescuing ciliogenesis in Ift80 null-mutant cells to the same degree as an untagged construct (Figures 7C and 8).
evidence: This statement describes rescue experiment data shown in Figures 7C and 8.

claim: Six missense mutations in IFT80 have been identified as causative in eight individuals with JATD.
source: Currently, six missense mutations in IFT80 have been identified as causative in eight individuals with JATD, each of which is private to individual families.
evidence: This statement describes clinical genetic data.

claim: No clear differences in clinical severity are noted between JATD patients with different IFT80 mutations either between or within families.
source: No clear differences in clinical severity are noted between patients either between or within families.
evidence: This statement describes clinical observations.

claim: All residues affected by IFT80 missense mutations are completely conserved in vertebrates and well conserved in C. reinhardtii.
source: All residues affected by these mutations are completely conserved in vertebrates and well conserved in C. reinhardtii.
evidence: This statement describes sequence conservation analysis.

claim: p.H105Q, p.L143S and p.G241R mutations reside within BP1 of IFT80.
source: p.H105Q, p.L143S and p.G241R mutations reside within BP1 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–C), whereas the p.A701P and p.R719C mutations are located within the very C-terminal α-extension required for IFT54/20 binding (not observed in our crystal structure).
evidence: This statement describes structural mapping shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: p.A701P and p.R719C mutations are located within the very C-terminal α-extension required for IFT54/20 binding.
source: p.H105Q, p.L143S and p.G241R mutations reside within BP1 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–C), whereas the p.A701P and p.R719C mutations are located within the very C-terminal α-extension required for IFT54/20 binding (not observed in our crystal structure).
evidence: This statement describes structural mapping and makes an inference about the location.

claim: The p.L549del mutation is located at the very end of an α-helical extension found between β-strands β50 and β51 of BP2.
source: Interestingly, the p.L549del mutation is located at the very end of an α-helical extension found between β-strands β50 and β51 of BP2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This statement describes structural mapping shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: IFT80 missense mutations are distributed across different functional domains of the protein and are unlikely to affect dimerization.
source: Therefore, IFT80 missense mutations are distributed across different functional domains of the protein, and are unlikely to affect dimerization.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the structural mapping of mutations.

claim: All point mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP rescued cilia formation to the same degree as wild-type.
source: We next tested the ability of missense mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP to rescue ciliogenesis. All point mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP rescued cilia formation to the same degree as wild-type (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This statement describes rescue experiment data shown in Figure 8.

claim: All missense mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP localised to puncta within the ciliary axoneme.
source: We also found that all missense mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP localised to puncta within the ciliary axoneme, and quantification of the proportion of GFP +cilia revealed no difference to the wild-type (Figure 8B and D and Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement describes microscopy observations shown in figures.

claim: All transfected missense mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP were expressed at significantly lower levels than wild-type.
source: Western blotting showed that all transfected missense mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP were expressed at significantly lower levels than wild-type, suggesting that these mutations cause protein instability (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement describes Western blot data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Missense mutations in IFT80 cause protein instability.
source: Western blotting showed that all transfected missense mutant forms of mIFT80-GFP were expressed at significantly lower levels than wild-type, suggesting that these mutations cause protein instability (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is an inference from Western blot data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Point mutations in IFT80 found in JATD retain a significant degree of protein function with respect to ciliogenesis and IFT.
source: Collectively, these data confirm that point mutations in IFT80 found in JATD retain a significant degree of protein function with respect to ciliogenesis and IFT.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiment data.

claim: IFT801-657 provides a partial rescue with about half the amount of cells forming cilia compared to full-length IFT80 rescue.
source: The IFT801-657 construct that lacks the IFT54/20 binding domain but contains the IFT80 dimerization domain provides a partial rescue with about half the amount of cells forming cilia compared to the full-length IFT80 rescue (Figure 9B–C).
evidence: This statement describes rescue experiment data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The reduction of cilium formation in the IFT801-657 rescue experiment is likely a result of the reduced ability of this construct to bind IFT54/20.
source: The reduction of cilium formation in the IFT801-657 rescue experiment is likely a result of the reduced ability of this construct to bind IFT54/20 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement is an inference from the rescue data and binding data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: The IFT54/20 binding domain of IFT80 is not mandatory for initiation of ciliogenesis or IFT.
source: However, given that IFT80 is absolutely required for cilium formation in these cells, the partial rescue demonstrates that the IFT54/20 binding domain of IFT80 is not mandatory for initiation of ciliogenesis or IFT.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the partial rescue data.

claim: Cells expressing IFT80 constructs containing only BP1 (IFT801-300) or BP1-BP2 (IFT801-586) are completely unable to ciliate.
source: In contrast, cells expressing IFT80 constructs containing only BP1 (IFT801-300) or BP1-BP2 (IFT801-586) are completely unable to ciliate (Figure 9B–C), demonstrating that the C-terminal α-helical domain of IFT80 is essential for cilium formation.
evidence: This statement describes rescue experiment data shown in Figure 9.

claim: The C-terminal α-helical domain of IFT80 is essential for cilium formation.
source: In contrast, cells expressing IFT80 constructs containing only BP1 (IFT801-300) or BP1-BP2 (IFT801-586) are completely unable to ciliate (Figure 9B–C), demonstrating that the C-terminal α-helical domain of IFT80 is essential for cilium formation.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from rescue experiment data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Both IFT801-300 and IFT801-586 constructs contain the BP1 domain that links IFT80 to the IFT complex via IFT38.
source: Both IFT801-300 an IFT801-586 constructs contain the BP1 domain that links IFT80 to the IFT complex via IFT38 (Figure 3).
evidence: This statement describes the domain composition of constructs based on earlier data.

claim: The inability of IFT801-586 to rescue ciliogenesis is not a direct result of IFT80 not associating with the IFT complex.
source: The inability of IFT801-586 to rescue ciliogenesis is thus not a direct result of IFT80 not associating with the IFT complex.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the rescue data and binding data.

claim: Residues 587–657 of IFT80, which are required for IFT80 dimerization, appear to be essential for cilium formation.
source: As IFT801-586 fails to rescues ciliogenesis and IFT801-657 provides a partial rescue of ciliogenesis (Figure 9B–C), residues 587–657, which are required for IFT80 dimerization (Figure 6), thus appear to be essential for cilium formation.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the rescue data and dimerization data.

claim: IFT80 homodimerization is required for cilium formation in mammalian cells.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that IFT80 homodimerization is required for cilium formation in mammalian cells.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiment data.

claim: The IFT80 dimerization observed in the crystal structure has 2-fold symmetry and could constitute the molecular basis of IFT particle doublet formation.
source: The dimerization of IFT80 observed in the crystal structure presented here has 2-fold symmetry and could thus constitute the molecular basis of IFT particle doublet formation.
evidence: This statement is a speculation based on the crystal structure and EM observations.

claim: IFT80 dimerization is unlikely to form the basis for train formation along the axonemal axis, as this relies on an asymmetric interface.
source: The IFT80 dimerization is, however, unlikely to form the basis for train formation along the axonemal axis, as this relies on an asymmetric interface (Pigino et al., 2009) (Figure 10).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the crystal structure and cited EM data shown in Figure 10.

claim: Reconstituted IFT-B complexes containing IFT80 do not appear to form very long 'train-like' oligomers.
source: This notion agrees with the observation that reconstituted IFT-B complexes containing IFT80 do not appear to form very long 'train-like' oligomers (Figure 6C–E) (Taschner et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement describes observations from biophysical data and is supported by a citation.

claim: The mechanisms and proteins involved in IFT particle oligomerization into trains along the axonemal axis are currently not known.
source: Currently, the mechanisms and proteins involved in IFT particle oligomerization into trains along the axonemal axis are not known.
evidence: This statement explicitly acknowledges a gap in current knowledge.

claim: IFT particle oligomerization along the axonemal axis could be the result of association of IFT-B with factors such as the IFT-A complex or IFT motors.
source: It is tempting to speculate that this oligomerisation could be the result of association of IFT-B with factors such as the IFT-A complex or IFT motors.
evidence: This statement is explicitly identified as speculation.

claim: One possibility is that each fully assembled IFT-B complex contains two copies of IFT80, but only one copy of the other IFT-B proteins.
source: One possibility is that each fully assembled IFT-B complex contains two copies of IFT80, but only one copy of the other IFT-B proteins.
evidence: This statement presents a speculative possibility.

claim: Reconstitutions of IFT-B2 and IFT-B complexes appear to contain stoichiometric amounts of all subunits, including IFT80.
source: Firstly, judging from previous reconstitutions of both a 6-subunit IFT-B2 complex as well as of a 15-subunit IFT-B (B1 and B2) complex, these assemblies appear to contain stoichiometric amounts of all subunits, including IFT80 (Taschner et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: ITC data reveal a 1:1 IFT80:IFT38 complex.
source: Secondly, the ITC data displayed in Figure 3D reveal a 1:1 IFT80:IFT38 complex.
evidence: This statement describes ITC data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Only 1 copy of IFT80 is present per IFT-B complex, but the entire IFT-B complex can dimerize via the IFT80 subunit.
source: The second possibility is that only 1 copy of IFT80 is present per IFT-B complex, but that the entire IFT-B complex can dimerize via the IFT80 subunit.
evidence: This statement presents a speculative possibility.

claim: The IFT80 dimer structure is compatible with incorporation into the IFT complex as the N-terminal β-propeller is available to interact with IFT38.
source: This possibility is compatible with the IFT80 dimer shown in Figure 4 as the most N-terminal β-propeller is available to interact with IFT38 thus allowing incorporation of an IFT80 dimer into the IFT complex.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the crystal structure shown in Figure 4.

claim: The exact molecular basis of IFT train formation will have to await structural elucidation of higher order IFT complexes.
source: However, the exact molecular basis of IFT train formation will have to await the structural elucidation of higher order IFT complexes by X-ray crystallography, single particle EM or high-resolution EM tomographic reconstructions of isolated or reconstituted IFT trains.
evidence: This statement explicitly acknowledges the need for future structural studies.

claim: Missense mutations in IFT80 do not ablate IFT-B complex interactions or homodimerization of the protein.
source: Taken together, these observations suggest that missense mutations do not ablate IFT-B complex interactions or homodimerization of the protein.
evidence: This statement is an inference from the rescue and localization data.

claim: Missense mutations in IFT80 likely cause partial protein instability to a degree that is consistent with recruitment of cargo to cilia and IFT.
source: Given the genetic threshold relationship between IFT80 dosage and ciliogenesis (Rix et al., 2011), it is more likely that missense mutations cause partial protein instability to a degree that is consistent with recruitment of cargo to cilia and IFT.
evidence: This statement is an inference supported by a citation to a genetic study.
